Uttar Pradesh Widow Pension Scheme: Current Benefits, Eligibility, and Proposed Increase to Rs 1,500

28 Oct 2026, 01:55 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Public Services Desk · Source: www.indiatoday.in

2 min read

Key takeawaysThe Uttar Pradesh government provides a monthly pension of Rs 1,000 to eligible widows and destitute women through the Niradhar (Nirashrit) Mahila Pension scheme, commonly referred to as the Vidhwa Pension. This initiative aims to offer financial support to women who have lost their spouses and lack steady income sources.

Overview of the Scheme

The Uttar Pradesh government provides a monthly pension of Rs 1,000 to eligible widows and destitute women through the Niradhar (Nirashrit) Mahila Pension scheme, commonly referred to as the Vidhwa Pension. This initiative aims to offer financial support to women who have lost their spouses and lack steady income sources.

Current Pension Amount and Disbursement

Beneficiaries currently receive Rs 1,000 per month, which is directly transferred into their bank accounts. The scheme is part of the state’s broader social security framework, targeting vulnerable sections of society.

Eligibility Criteria

To qualify for the pension, applicants must meet the following conditions:

  • Residency: Must be a permanent resident of Uttar Pradesh.
  • Income Limit: Annual household income from all sources must not exceed Rs 2 lakh.
  • Exclusivity: Applicants cannot be receiving a pension under any other state or central government scheme.

Application Process

Interested individuals can apply online via the Uttar Pradesh government’s social security pension portal. Required documents include:

  • Income certificate
  • Aadhaar details
  • Bank account information
  • Death certificate of the spouse (for widows)

Proposed Pension Increase

Media reports in October 2026 indicated that the Uttar Pradesh government is considering raising the monthly pension from Rs 1,000 to Rs 1,500 for beneficiaries under the old-age, destitute women’s, and disability pension schemes. However, this proposal remains under review and requires Cabinet approval and formal implementation orders. As of now, the Rs 1,000 monthly amount remains unchanged.

The combined beneficiary count for these three categories exceeds 1.21 crore, according to the reports. The destitute women’s pension, which includes widows, forms a subset of this figure.

Practical Implications

For many women, particularly those without a steady income or in households with no earning members, the pension serves as a critical lifeline for meeting basic expenses. If the proposed increase is approved, it could significantly enhance the financial stability of over 1 crore beneficiaries. However, the timeline and certainty of this change remain unclear until official notifications are issued.

Verification and Further Information

Readers can verify eligibility criteria, application procedures, and updates through the official Uttar Pradesh social security pension portal. The government’s announcements and press releases will provide definitive details on any policy changes. For real-time updates, monitoring state government websites or contacting local social welfare departments is recommended.

Background on the Scheme

The Vidhwa Pension scheme is designed to address gender-based economic disparities, ensuring widowed women have access to essential resources. It aligns with broader efforts to promote social welfare and reduce poverty among marginalized communities in the state.
